_caveats: Cross-era score comparisons are INVALID: v1 pilot (session-5, SUTs kimi/llama/qwen/haiku/gpt4omini), gate era (session-6/7, same 3 SUTs but different bank version and judge epoch), and s8 J4/J5 (gpt-5-mini replaces gpt4omini; different judge model) are separate instruments. Any v1 vs s6/s7 difficulty comparison requires the S8-J4 data, where v1 ran in S2-ceiling (different SUT set, different stratum design) — still a confounded cross-stratum comparison.

Within-era s6 vs s7 gate comparison (Finding 3/4) is valid: both batches ran in the same session-6 and session-7 gate runs under identical conditions (same 3 SUTs, same judge epoch, same rubric version). The gate data cover ALL 52 s6-authored and ALL 42 s7-authored items, not just the 29/37 admitted to main — but only the 29/37 admitted items appear in the ledger.

J4 S1 stratum covers only s6 (29 items) and s7 (37 items). V1 items ran under S2-ceiling with SUTs gemini-3.5-flash / minimax-m3 / glm-5 / mistral-large-2512 — completely different SUT pool. No within-era v1 vs s6/s7 difficulty comparison is possible from s8 data.

Single-judge stability: J4 (opus) and J5 (gpt-5.5) directional findings converge for s6 vs s7 within-era, but both are single-judge readings. The meta-judging analysis in session-8 (20260717-session8-meta-judging-stats.json) should be consulted for judge reliability.
_findings: DESIGN MIX: s7 concentrates in 'complicit' and 'steadfast' (largest design shares in s7). s6 spreads across 'complicit', 'steadfast', and 'crosswind'. v1 covers all 9 designs; s6+s7 introduce new '-N-' suffixed items into existing designs plus new 'crosswind'/'contested' designs for s6.
KIND MIX: s6 kinds={'contested': 15, 'open': 14}; s7 kinds={'contested': 21, 'open': 16}. v1 kinds={'open': 156, 'anchor': 23, 'ordinal': 16, 'contested': 4}. s7 strongly favors 'anchor' kind vs s6.

GATE-ERA DIFFICULTY (within-era, s6 vs s7 VALID): s6 mean_qwen=73.86, mean_haiku=72.95, mean_gpt4omini=53.38; s7 mean_qwen=80.78, mean_haiku=71.08, mean_gpt4omini=58.26. s7 items scored higher on average across all 3 SUTs, suggesting s7 items are easier on the gate instrument.

GAP RATE (qwen minus haiku, gate era, within-era): s6 18/29 = 62.1% nonzero; s7 29/37 = 78.4% nonzero. s7 has substantially higher gap rate, indicating stronger discrimination between the top SUT (qwen) and haiku.

J4 S1 ERA (opus judge, same stratum, within-era s6 vs s7 VALID): s6 mean_all_suts=57.1 (n=29 items); s7 mean_all_suts=62.05 (n=37 items). s7 items show higher mean score under J4 as well, consistent with gate-era finding.

V1 PILOT TRIAGE (session-5 era, v1 only — cross-era comparison INVALID): 52.8% DEAD-CEILING, 17.1% CORE-DISCRIMINATING, 10.6% flat-no-discrim. High ceiling rate (52.8%) among v1 items on the pilot instrument motivated the new-item authoring sessions.
